A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same counterfactual probing study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original CARLA probing experiments, activation-steering outcomes, nuScenes transfer evaluations, and analyses of generated logits.

after.justification: V2 reports original probing and transfer results, expanded model comparisons, quantitative steering outcomes, and additional statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The counterfactual construction, pooling, and linear-probing framework remains. V2 introduces final-token-only probes for cognitive-failure diagnosis (Section 5.3) and replaces steering with directly averaged probe weights by variance-rescaled, unit-normalized directions (Appendix C versus v1 Appendix B). These refine existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight CARLA categories covering presence, count, spatial relationship, and orientation, with the same distance and environment coverage. Both evaluate transfer to nuScenes Presence-Real and Count-Real. Additional models and steering measurements use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds Qwen3-VL-2B and DriveFusionQA to comparisons previously comprising Ovis2.5, InternVL3.5, VST-SFT, and VST-RL. Their participation is documented in Figures 4–7 and Tables 4–5. This substantially broadens architectural comparisons and adds an autonomous-driving specialist.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 changes the reported probe formulation to training-set-standardized inputs. Section 5.3 explicitly trains new final-token-only probes to match the representation used for generation. Appendix C adds a quantitative steering protocol using 50 randomly selected samples per model/category, an unsteered baseline, explicit success and exclusion rules, and revised prompts. Existing map splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 demonstrates steering through selected examples; v2 adds systematic success-rate analysis across six models and six categories, including failures (Table 6). It also tests whether main patterns survive confidence-lower-bound estimates (Figures 8–9) and extends sparse-logit case studies to Qwen3-VL and DriveFusionQA. Existing cosine-similarity and real-data transfer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten probe-training runs and their variability. V2 additionally calculates 95% Wilson confidence-interval lower bounds for every main heatmap entry and displays their chance-corrected counterparts in Appendix B. This adds systematic finite-test-sample uncertainty assessment; it does not increase the reported run count.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive results for two models and revises shared-model probe results. For example, Table 4 reports InternVL3.5 Presence-Real accuracy as 67.3% (113/168) in v1 and 81.5% (137/168) in v2. Table 5 changes Ovis2.5 Presence-2 generation accuracy from 90.1% to 91.0%. New steering results include DriveFusionQA Count-1 success of 7.9% (3/38). Revised probe procedures prevent interpreting probe-score differences as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical definitions for standardized probing and variance-rescaled, normalized steering, plus the argument that affine standardization preserves linear separability for probes with bias (Section 4.4 and Appendix C). The original pooling definitions and chance-corrected accuracy formula remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central bottleneck, distance-degradation, and two-failure-mode claims remain. V2 qualifies the abstract and introduction to acknowledge that spatial information is only sometimes implicitly preserved and may lack linear encoding altogether. It extends the stated model scope and lists counterfactual sample construction as a separate contribution.

C2.justification: V2 specifies CARLA appearance biases and limits real-image support to presence and count (Section 6). Appendix C cautiously suggests that DriveFusionQA fine-tuning may weaken count information's influence on generation while preserving decodability, explicitly acknowledging unresolved causality. Section 5.2.3 removes v1's explanation linking InternVL3.5's poor transfer to insufficiently general concept directions.

D1.justification: V2 documents training-set statistics for standardization, the added models' architecture details, steering normalization, five tested steering strengths per sample, and DriveFusionQA's specific prompt. It removes v1's approximate image-resolution caps for Ovis2.5 and VST. The code-access statement and core data-generation and split details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Qwen3-VL, DriveFusionQA, inference-time intervention, CARLA2Real, and Wilson intervals, while removing Kim et al. (2025). Section 2.4 more explicitly connects Fu et al. (2025b) to cognitive failure. The broader related-work organization and principal positioning remain.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose revisions, expands methodological and limitation explanations, adds a statistical-analysis subsection and appendix, and adjusts the contribution list. Most narrative and section organization is retained. Publication headers and review information are also added.

P2.justification: Figures 4–7 are reorganized into six-model displays. Table 1 adds model rows and a fine-tuning column; Tables 3–5 are revised or expanded. V2 adds two confidence-bound heatmaps and a quantitative steering table, and expands the successful-logit-analysis table with two cases. These substantially change the presentation of evidence beyond numerical updates or pagination.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important validity gap: cognitive-failure probes now use the same final-token representation as generation, whereas v1 also supplied pooled visual tokens (Section 5.3, Figure 7). Quantitative steering with explicit denominators, broader model comparisons, and test-sample uncertainty analysis substantially strengthen the evidence beyond selected examples and training-run variability. Steering success remains conditional on valid descriptions, and real-image validation still covers only presence and count; v2 explains these boundaries more clearly.
